title: AI Agents, Tool Use & MCP: Building Agents That Stay in Their Lane
concept: Build agents only where a fixed workflow is not enough, and keep them safe: narrow tools with clear schemas, MCP servers for internal data, an agent loop you can test with a fake model, audit logs, step and budget limits, read-freely-write-with-approval permissions, and tool output treated as data rather than instructions.
description: An expert course for engineers putting LLM agents next to real data and real actions. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a support ticket that told the agent to refund every order and it called the write tool, an agent that looped for 40 minutes on a failing tool, a tool description so vague the model passed a learner's email as a course id, an MCP server that exposed the whole database - and fixes it with code you can test against a scripted fake model: workflow or agent, tool design, the agent loop, MCP basics and an internal-data server, audit logs, step limits, budgets, a Spot the AI Mistake loop that never stops, permission policies, untrusted tool output, The Agent Went Rogue scenario, workflow tools versus code, multi-agent patterns and evaluating agents. 15 lessons with True/False quizzes on real transcripts and tool calls, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Decide when an agent is worth it and when a fixed workflow is enough
Design narrow tools and MCP servers with clear schemas and audit every call
Bound agents with step, token and time limits and stop conditions
Enforce least privilege: read freely, write with approval, and treat tool output as untrusted data
Run, observe and evaluate agents with a fake model, audit logs and transcripts
